item.title: Diabolique — That Boy Hi Hat
item.description: "Diabolique" is a slow-burning nocturnal record that sits at the dark heart of That Boy Hi Hat's catalog. Over a halftime trap pulse at 77 BPM in G-sharp minor, the production — co-produced by Hybrid and Black Lansky — builds a widescreen, cinematic soundscape: foggy atmospheric synth pads, sparse but hard-hitting drums, and a low 808-driven undertow that keeps the whole track leaning forward like a scene shot in slow motion. This is alternative rap at its most seductive and most dangerous. item.description: "Bluefaces 3.0" is King Ahkeem at his most confident — a trap record co-produced by Black Lansky that treats the money anthem as a contact sport. item.description: "Element" strips King Ahkeem's sound down to its foundation — a trap record co-produced by Black Lansky built on the idea that the basics, done right, hit hardest. item.description: "Embiid" is King Ahkeem playing at MVP level — a trap record co-produced by Black Lansky named for dominance and built to sound like it. item.title: Super Solid — King Ahkeem
item.description: "Super Solid" is King Ahkeem's oath of reliability — a trap record co-produced by Black Lansky about being the one thing that doesn't crack under pressure. The title is a promise, and the track delivers it with a confident, aggressive stride and a hype energy that feels earned rather than performed. The beat is trap built like concrete — the sub-heavy 808 bass drives the track throughout, locked to crisp hi-hats that snap in the chorus, with dark synth stabs and snare hits providing the structural reinforcement, and atmospheric pads filling the gaps so the whole thing feels dense and immovable
